title: Ops health brain-dump for SRE weekly sync
content:
Context and goal:
- Quick prep notes for Tue SRE ops sync (30m). This is messy — use as scratch, prune into meeting notes after sync.
- Goal: align on SLOs, recurring paging trends, and top 2 incidents to track to remediation. Leave ~10m for tactical decisions.

Data to grab before the call (front-load):
- Error budget burn rate (7d and 30d) for hosted-api model endpoints (hosted-us & hosted-eu). Pull from dashboard: 'slo/availability/hosted-api/v1' and 'slo/latency/p99'.
- Pager volume by rule for last 14 days (alerts broken down: infra oom / serving-timeouts / model-compile-failures / route-throttles). Grafana panel: 'alerts/pager-volume-by-rule'.
- KV cache hit ratio + eviction rate by model shard (last 24h). Quick hypothesis: eviction spikes correlate with p99 latency spikes.
- Token generation latency distribution split by: cached prefix vs cold-start (no KV).

Agenda (rough, re-order as needed):
1) Quick status (2m): outstanding escalations, team capacity (who's oncall next week).
2) SLO health (8m): 7d/30d burn, any SLO close to alerting, priority SLOs to protect this week.
3) Paging trends (6m): top noisy alerts, candidate suppression/aggregation, immediate mitigations.
4) Top incidents (8m): review incident timelines & action items for last 2 weeks (see incident summaries below).
5) Runbook gaps & automation ideas (3m): who can own?
6) Action items and owners (3m).

Notes / observations (scratch):
- Hosted EU had 2 short severity-2 latency bursts on 2026-03-12 around 11:20 & 14:05. Both correlate with KV-cache eviction spikes and sudden batch size bumps from a test tenant. Hypothesis: aggressive batch config from test workload pushed memory, causing compaction/eviction.
- Pager count trending +18% week-over-week; majority are timeouts and 'model-compile-failure' alerts. A few of those compile failures are transient (retry succeeds) — consider reducing page severity and convert to internal ticket for 3x transient failures.
- p99 latency for small completion (<128 tokens) is stable in us-west, but eu p99 increases when prefix cache miss > 15%.

Top incidents (brief):
- INC-2026-03-12-EU-LAT: Partial degradation hosted-eu. Timeline:
  * 11:15 - small increase in 5xx and p99 latency.
  * 11:17 - alert: serving-timeouts (rule: serve.timeout.5xx).
  * 11:18 - oncall check; KV cache eviction rate elevated; several hosts reporting memory compaction logs.
  * 11:30 - roll back recent autoscaler patch on staging->prod (suspected mis-tuned batch size).
  * 12:05 - metrics recovering; follow-up: revert autoscaler change, add guardrail to enforce batch-size max per tenant.
  Open actions: create test that simulates concurrent small-batch bursts (owner: Omar, due: 2026-03-24).

- INC-2026-03-08-COMP-FALSEPOS: Model compilation failures spike overnight, most succeed on retry.
  * Root cause: temporary GPU driver update mismatch on a subset of nodes. Fixed by re-deploying driver image.
  * Follow-up: add alert to flag >3 failures/min for same model (currently threshold is 10). (owner: Liam, due: 2026-03-21)

Paging trends + quick fixes:
- Noise sources: low-threshold compile-fail alerts, route-throttles when autoscaler slowly spins up, and periodic healthcheck flapping on old nodes.
- Quick mitigations to propose:
  1) Aggregation window for compile-failures: 3m -> 6m before paging if failures are same model id.
  2) Add a cooldown on route-throttle paging: allow 1 retry window before paging.
  3) Healthcheck flapping: increase success threshold from 2 -> 3 to reduce transient pages.

Runbook / automation gaps:
- No automated rollback/scale-down when host memory compaction > 60% and eviction rate > X. Need a small automation to reduce batch sizes for high-memory tenants automatically.
- Runbook for 'model-compile-failure' lacks clear severity mapping and retry policy.
- No dedicated playbook for KV-cache saturation event — add one.

Action items (to capture during meeting):
- AI-001: Omar to create reproducible load test for batch-spike scenario, include tenant-level throttling toggle. (owner: Omar Patel, due: 2026-03-24)
- AI-002: Liam to tighten compile-failure alert thresholds and add aggregation rule (owner: Liam O'Connor, due: 2026-03-21).
- AI-003: Maya to draft KV-cache saturation runbook and commit to repo (owner: Maya Chen, due: 2026-03-26).
- AI-004: Emily (product infra) to weigh in on customer-facing change to batch-size limits (ask in PRD thread) — @Emily via slack. (ask by 2026-03-20)
- AI-005: Ops automation spike to evaluate auto-reduce-batch feature (owner: eng-infra rotation, add to sprint backlog).

Questions to raise in sync:
- Product: Are there any tenants with intentional high-concurrency tests that we should cordon off?
- SRE leadership: Can we deprioritize paging for one-off transient compile failures until we have aggregation in place?
- Observability: Can we add a small panel for 'prefix cache miss ratio' per-region for triage?

Stuff to bring to the call (links):
- Grafana: hosted-api SLO dashboard (bookmark), alerts/pager-volume-by-rule, kv-cache-metrics.
- Incident writeups: INC-2026-03-12-EU-LAT (confluence) and INC-2026-03-08-COMP-FALSEPOS.
- Recent PRs: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/5123 (autoscaler change)

Notes to self (last-minute):
- Start meeting by confirming no active Sev1s. If there is one, shift to incident response.
- Keep suggestions pragmatic; propose temporary mitigations where full fix is >2 sprints.
- After sync: convert this doc into a tidy meeting notes doc and move to shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/weekly-notes.

End of brain-dump.
